transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ava (Head of ML, MedicaLens), Raj (CTO), Tom (Infra), Maya (PM)

Summary (auto):
Redwood and MedicaLens scoped a POC to validate inference scalability and latency for a medical-imaging assisted triage service. Primary focus was traffic modelling: QPS, concurrency, input/output token distributions (text prompts + small metadata), and success criteria for acceptance (p90 latency, throughput, cost threshold). Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: POC goals; workload profile; benchmark plan; security & data residency; timelines and success criteria; integration check points.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick round-robin — can we go names and roles?
[00:12] Ava Chen: Ava here, Head of ML at MedicaLens. We own the triage model and the infra requirements.
[00:17] Raj Patel: Raj, CTO, mostly here for the infra and compliance questions.
[00:21] Tom Garcia: Tom, infra engineer, I'll pull logs and help with the pilot.
[00:25] Maya Ortiz: Maya, product manager, focused on timelines and success criteria.
[00:28] Lena Martinez: Awesome. Omar and Priya from Redwood are with me. Quick agenda: align on target workload (QPS/concurrency), define acceptance criteria, scope benchmarks and timelines, and list out security blockers.
[00:43] Omar Singh: For context, we typically model three traffic modes: steady-state (low qps), bursty peak (short spikes), and scheduled batch for nightly re-runs. We'll need histograms for input lengths and output lengths, and a sense of concurrency per user session.
[00:58] Ava Chen: Our prod expectation: 30 sustained QPS during business hours, spikes up to 220 QPS for short windows (1-3 min) when clinics sync. Most requests are small: prompt is 40-80 tokens on average, outputs are 80-160 tokens. But some EMR-augmented prompts can go to 400 tokens.
[01:20] Priya Rao: Thanks, Ava. Do you have token length percentiles? 50/90/99?
[01:26] Ava Chen: We have a rough export: p50=62 tokens in, p90=180 in, p99~420 in. Out p50=95, p90=210, p99=460. I'll share exact CSVs.
[01:40] Raj Patel: Important: data residency — all inference must occur in our VPC in us-east-1 and no raw PHI leaves the VPC. KMS-managed keys only.
[01:50] Lena Martinez: Got it. For the POC we can run Redwood Private in your VPC or we can use a dedicated-hosted lane if you prefer not to onboard private control plane. Tom, which is easier?
[02:02] Tom Garcia: Short-term, dedicated-hosted is faster. Long term we'll want the Private deployment. For POC we want to validate both latency SLA and the encryption-in-flight to our KMS.
[02:12] Omar Singh: Ok. For benchmark plan we suggest: baseline latency profile (p50/p90/p99) at 30 QPS steady; ramp tests to 220 QPS spike; and sustained 100 QPS for 1 hour to measure throughput and memory/KV cache behavior. We'll collect GPU utilization and hop counts.
[02:34] Maya Ortiz: Also cost targets — our CFO wants < $0.003 per inference average under production mix, roughly. Is that realistic with your batching and quantization?
[02:45] Omar Singh: We can definitely model cost with different quantization profiles. For mix with average token counts you mentioned, using int8/4-bit quantization and responsible batching we often hit sub-$0.0025 in dedicated environments. But it depends on beam/temperature and rechunking.
[03:00] Ava Chen: Important nuance: Latency SLO is p90 < 250ms for the majority of calls. Some diagnostic calls can be longer. We need to make sure batching doesn't push p90 above 250.
[03:13] Priya Rao: We can configure latency targets per route and do autoscale policies with cold-warm pools. For p90 250ms we will set low batch windows and enable prefix/KV caching for session-based tokens to reduce cost.
[03:27] Raj Patel: How much instrumentation do you need? We want token-level tracing and redwood to send metrics to our Prometheus/Grafana.
[03:36] Lena Martinez: Redwood Console supports export to Prometheus and we can include token-level breakdowns per route. We'll provide a short trace hook to Knative or your pipeline. Note: automatic tracing labels sometimes mangle acronyms — we'll double check that for you.
[03:49] Tom Garcia: For the POC data, we'll sanitize PHI but keep token length distributions. We'll provide ~48 hours of traffic logs for the week of the test.
[03:59] Omar Singh: Great. A quick question on concurrency model: are requests single-shot or streaming?
[04:05] Ava Chen: Mostly single-shot, but a small subset — about 8% — use streaming for progressive results to clients.
[04:13] Priya Rao: That changes server-side concurrency. For streaming we need to keep KV cache warmed for sessions; it increases memory per connection. We'll note that in infra sizing.
[04:25] [00:04:25] Speaker 3: (unintelligible)
[04:30] Raj Patel: On timeline, we're targeting an internal pilot sign-off in mid-August. So POC needs to complete by first week of August to allow two weeks of product validation.
[04:41] Lena Martinez: So tentatively POC window: 2025-07-28 to 2025-08-03 for the benchmark run. We'll need your logs by 2025-07-18.
[04:52] Ava Chen: That works. We'll aim to deliver compressed logs and token histograms by the 18th.
[04:58] Omar Singh: For workload sizing, preliminary numbers we propose: for steady-state 30 QPS with concurrency 30, each request average 120 input tokens and 140 output tokens; dedupe the 8% streaming as separate route. For spikes, provision for 250 concurrent connections and autoscale to handle 220 QPS for 3 minutes.
[05:20] Maya Ortiz: Can you simulate clinic sync events that cause higher concurrency and cold-cache penalties?
[05:25] Omar Singh: Yes, we'll run a synthetic traffic generator that replays your logs and introduces cold prefixes to measure cold-warm behavior.
[05:33] Ava Chen: Another requirement: audit logs for inference inputs flagged as PHI need to be redacted and only hashes stored. Can we verify redaction in POC?
[05:43] Lena Martinez: We'll include redaction verification steps. Redwood Private supports field-level masking and KMS-based key rotation; we'll share the doc.
[05:52] Raj Patel: Liability/contract note — if we hit regression in answer quality after model quantization we'll need rollback and evaluation metrics.
[05:59] Priya Rao: Absolutely. We'll run evals against your holdout prompt set pre- and post-quantization and provide BLEU/ROUGE style summary metrics plus human spot checks.
[06:12] [00:06:12] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[06:18] Tom Garcia: Operational question: what hardware are you planning to use during the POC? GPU types?
[06:23] Omar Singh: For the Dedicated lane we'll use A100 80GB for the heavier models. For some tests we can use 1/2 quantized variants on T4s to test cost tradeoffs. If we run Redwood Private in your VPC you can map to your on-prem cluster or we can bring a cloud-hosted private VPC with the chosen instance types.
[06:40] Ava Chen: Can you show an example of the latency breakdown — tokenization, KV cache, model forward — so we can see where tail latency arises?
[06:47] Priya Rao: Yes, each sample includes: request parsing, tokenization, prefix cache lookup (if applicable), attention compute, and post-processing. We'll instrument and plot p50/p90/p99 for each phase.
[06:58] Lena Martinez: Speaking of tails, do you have any outlier requests that cause huge contexts? Those can bust KV cache assumptions.
[07:05] Ava Chen: Occasionally a clinician attaches a long summary — maybe up to 6K tokens — but that's rare. We'll flag those as a separate heavy route and exclude them from main latency SLO.
[07:16] Omar Singh: Good, we'll treat heavy route as its own traffic class with separate scaling.
[07:22] [00:07:22] Speaker 4: (murmur)
[07:26] Raj Patel: Security: SOC2 in place? How about penetration tests and external audits?
[07:31] Lena Martinez: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant. We can share the attestation and the security pack. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options.
[07:41] Tom Garcia: KMS integration: we need key rotation policy and logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[07:46] Priya Rao: We'll provide a KMS integration checklist and a sample terraform snippet. Logs can be forwarded via Fluentd to your SIEM.
[07:55] Maya Ortiz: On success criteria, product wants: p90 latency <250ms for main route, end-to-end availability > 99.8% across the test window, and less than 5% regression in answer quality against baseline. Also the CFO cost threshold mentioned earlier.
[08:12] Lena Martinez: We'll codify those as acceptance criteria in the POC SOW.
[08:16] Omar Singh: Benchmarks we'll run: 1) Steady 30 QPS for 3 hours; 2) Spike test — ramp to 220 QPS for 3 minutes repeated 6 times over an hour; 3) Long-run at 100 QPS for 1 hour to stress KV cache; 4) Quality eval on 2k prompts across the model/quantization variants.
[08:38] Ava Chen: For the quality eval, we will provide the holdout set and the rubric. We also want an example of hallucination metrics or confidence scores.
[08:48] Priya Rao: We'll include hallucination detection heuristics and the eval reports.
[08:52] [00:08:52] Speaker 1: (laughter)
[08:55] Tom Garcia: For the synthetic replay, do you need per-request headers or just the body?
[08:59] Omar Singh: Ideally headers that impact caching (user-id, session-id, route) and timing stamps. But if you can provide sanitized headers and bodies with timestamps that's enough.
[09:11] Raj Patel: About costs — if we run dedicated vs private what's the expected delta?
[09:16] Omar Singh: Dedicated hosted lumps infra into a committed monthly rate; unit compute cost for tokens is lower in dedicated compared to pay-as-you-go hosted. Private has higher upfront onboarding but can lower unit cost if you bring your own infra; depends on utilization. We'll run a cost model in the template.
[09:34] Ava Chen: Do you have prior benchmarks for medical-language models? I'm worried about clinical language nuances.
[09:40] Priya Rao: We have internal benchmarks and some open-med datasets; we'll run domain-specific evals once you share your holdout. Clinical language sometimes increases perplexity modestly and can affect generation length.
[09:52] Lena Martinez: Ok let's talk deliverables and dates.
[09:56] Mia Ortiz: (typo) Maya Ortiz: We need POC SOW, benchmark template, and the security pack.
[10:03] Lena Martinez: We'll send SOW draft and benchmark template by 2025-07-16. Omar will prepare config recommendations and batching suggestions by 7/21.
[10:11] Omar Singh: For the POC run, we'll ask for a 48-hour window where we run multiple test scenarios. The actual heavy benchmark day will be 2025-07-29.
[10:20] Ava Chen: Can we include a canary step where we route 5% of live traffic to Redwood Dedicated during the test?
[10:27] Priya Rao: Yes, but we'll need a rollback plan and safe-guards. Also a circuit-breaker config to avoid PHI leakage.
[10:36] Raj Patel: Legal will want a data processing addendum (DPA) that covers PHI handling.
[10:40] Lena Martinez: We'll attach the DPA draft to the SOW.
[10:44] [00:10:44] Speaker 2: (background noise)
[10:47] Tom Garcia: A quick note on metrics — we'll want request-level latency, token counts, GPU usage, batch sizes, cache hits, and traces for any p99 outliers. Can Redwood export all of that?
[10:59] Priya Rao: Yes, all of those metrics are available. Some fields are opt-in but we'll enable them for the POC.
[11:06] Maya Ortiz: Success sign-off — who signs? Product + ML lead + Infra?
[11:10] Ava Chen: Product and ML will sign, infra will provide go/no-go for private deployment.
[11:15] Lena Martinez: Good. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[11:18] Raj Patel: Contract review timeline — legal needs two weeks to review SOW and DPA.
[11:23] Lena Martinez: We'll send docs 7/16, that gives legal two weeks before the pilot.
[11:28] Ava Chen: Small ask — can you include a low-touch demo of Redwood Console's per-route traces during the pilot?
[11:35] Lena Martinez: Yes, we'll include a guided console tour and a shared dashboard.
[11:40] Omar Singh: Ok, technical detail: for TK caching — are sessions sticky to user ids?
[11:45] Ava Chen: Yes, session-id mapping is stable for up to 48 hours.
[11:48] Priya Rao: That helps caching efficiency. We'll model a 48-hour cache TTL.
[11:53] [00:11:53] Speaker 3: (unintelligible)
[11:56] Tom Garcia: We'll aim to provide logs in gzipped JSON with timestamped events.
[12:02] Omar Singh: Perfect. Another detail: can you confirm the percent of requests that include attachments (images) vs text only?
[12:09] Ava Chen: Attachments are rare for the triage text path — maybe 3% — those go to a different pipeline.
[12:15] Priya Rao: We'll exclude image path from main benchmark.
[12:18] Raj Patel: Any specific SLAs for Dedicated?
[12:21] Lena Martinez: Dedicated comes with SLA targets for uptime and a latency SLO; we'll include the numbers in the SOW.
[12:28] Maya Ortiz: For the evaluation, can we get a sample of the post-quantization diffs per prompt? A diff heatmap would be helpful.
[12:36] Priya Rao: Yes, we'll include diffs and per-prompt scoring.
[12:40] Ava Chen: Regarding tooling, do you support on-the-fly rollback to float32 for a route if quality regresses?
[12:46] Omar Singh: We do — rollouts support model version pinning and automatic fallback to a float32 variant.
[12:51] [00:12:51] Speaker 1: (clears throat)
[12:54] Tom Garcia: Infrastructure sizing question — how many GPUs should we allocate for initial pilot?
[12:59] Omar Singh: For the steady and spike tests with the given token distributions I'd recommend starting with 4x A100 80GB, with autoscale to +2 for spikes, or 6x if you want single-digit ms headroom. We'll provide cost estimates.
[13:17] Raj Patel: If we do private on-prem, we only have V100s — will that be sufficient?
[13:22] Priya Rao: V100s can run smaller models or quantized variants, but peak throughput will be lower. We'll model it in the cost/throughput spreadsheet.
[13:31] Lena Martinez: Quick check — any regulatory constraints beyond PHI? EU data residency?
[13:35] Raj Patel: Not for this POC; it's US-only.
[13:38] Maya Ortiz: Timeline recap?
[13:40] Lena Martinez: Docs 7/16, logs 7/18, bench run week of 7/28, report by 8/04, internal sign-off mid-August.
[13:51] Ava Chen: That matches our internal cadence.
[13:54] [00:13:54] Speaker 4: (murmur)
[13:57] Tom Garcia: I'll create a ticket in our tracker to export the logs and invite Omar.
[14:02] Omar Singh: Thanks, Tom. We'll also prepare the synthetic replay harness and share the docker image for reproducing the test locally.
[14:10] Priya Rao: One more note — for the spike test we recommend a circuit-breaker threshold at 400ms p90 to avoid compromising downstream systems.
[14:20] Raj Patel: Sounds good.
[14:22] Lena Martinez: Anything else on the POC scope?
[14:25] Maya Ortiz: No, I think that's everything.
[14:28] Lena Martinez: Ok, we'll follow up with the SOW and benchmark template. Thanks everyone.
[14:33] Ava Chen: Thanks.
[14:34] Raj Patel: Thanks.
[14:35] Tom Garcia: Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription includes minor mis-hears (e.g., TK caching for KV cache in one snippet). Some speaker labels generic where recording quality dropped.
